name: Higher-Order Statistics
description: Analyzes kurtosis and skewness of gradient distributions. Natural images have heavy-tailed distributions while AI images tend toward Gaussian.
algorithm: Gradient Domain Kurtosis and Skewness Analysis
mechanism: Computes first-order gradient differences and analyzes their higher-order statistical moments. AI images show more Gaussian-like distributions.
useCase: Detecting Gaussian-like gradient statistics in AI-generated images

references.title: Lyu, S. & Farid, H. (2006). Steganalysis Using Higher-Order Image Statistics. IEEE TIFS.
Farid, H. (2009). Image Forgery Detection. IEEE Signal Processing Magazine.
Mendel, J.M. (1991). Tutorial on Higher-Order Statistics. Proceedings of the IEEE.

strengths:
• Captures non-Gaussian properties invisible to basic statistics
• Skewness and kurtosis reveal AI distribution anomalies
• Fast computation on pixel distributions
• Format-independent analysis
• Strong theoretical foundation in statistical signal processing
limitations:
• Lower standalone discrimination power
• Sensitive to image content type (sky vs complex scene)
• Post-processing can normalize distributions
• Requires sufficient image size for stable statistics
• Some AI models produce natural-looking distributions
